issues.title: Model builder: Gemma 3 sliding layers inherit the global layers RoPE linear scaling (rescale_factors)
Model builder: Mistral sliding_window dropped (no layer_types, every layer full attention), regression since 0.15.2

observations.scope:
I can confirm this. It came in with #2386 (first released in 0.16.0), which made the window per layer:

- `make_attention` now builds each layer with `self.window_size if self.is_local(layer_id) else -1` (`src/python/py/models/builders/base.py:5202`).
- `is_local` reads `self.layer_types`, and when the config has no `layer_types` the builder falls back to `["full_attention"] * self.num_layers` (`base.py:141-145`).

`MistralConfig` has no `layer_types` (4.57.6 and 5.22.1), so every layer gets `local_window_size = -1`. The same happens to `Phi3Config` with `sliding_window` set (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct has 2047) and to a `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` whose text config has a `sliding_window`. Configs that have `layer_types` (Qwen2, Gemma 2/3, gpt-oss, SmolLM3) are not affected.

The fix: when `layer_types` is missing, mark every layer `"sliding_attention"` if `sliding_window` is a positive int and `use_sliding_window` is not `False`, otherwise `"full_attention"`. This is what 0.15.2 did, and what transformers does for these models. I have a PR ready with unit tests (tiny Mistral/Phi-3/Qwen2 configs, no weights).

issues.title: Model builder: Gemma 3 fails with KeyError 'rope_type' under transformers 5
Model builder: Gemma 3's sliding-window layers get the global layers' linear RoPE scaling

observations.scope:
I looked into #2789/#2831 and #2788 together, since they are both in Gemma 3's RoPE setup.

#2789 (#2831 is the same): `Gemma3Model.make_rotary_embedding_multi_cache` (`src/python/py/models/builders/gemma.py:134-147`) builds the local caches after changing only `rope_attrs["theta"]` (line 142). `rope_attrs["rescale_factors"]` still holds the global linear factor set in `Model.make_rope_init` (`base.py:745`), so the local caches are scaled by 1/8 on Gemma 3 4B/12B/27B. transformers uses default, unscaled RoPE with `rope_local_base_freq` for the local layers (4.57.6: `rotary_emb_local` with `rope_scaling={"rope_type": "default"}`; 5.x: the `sliding_attention` entry, `rope_type: "default"`).

#2788: under transformers 5, Gemma 3's `rope_parameters` is nested per layer type, and the config no longer has `rope_theta` or `rope_local_base_freq`. `Model.make_rope_init` reads `config.rope_parameters["rope_type"]` (`base.py:717`) and raises `KeyError`. `Gemma3Model` has no `make_rope_init` of its own, unlike `Gemma4Model`.

Fix: `Gemma3Model.make_rope_init` reads the nested form (the `full_attention` entry for the global caches and their theta, and the `sliding_attention` theta for the local caches). `make_rotary_embedding_multi_cache` builds the local caches with `rescale_factors = 1` and no other global scaling, then restores the global RoPE attributes. I have a PR ready, with tests that compare the cos/sin caches against transformers' own Gemma 3 rotary embedding for the 4.x and 5.x config forms.
